From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Chris Jennings is an American journalist and author. He is a former editorial staffer at The New Yorker . [ 1 ] He is a graduate of Deep Springs College and Wesleyan University . [ 2 ]

* End of Days: Ruby Ridge, The Apocalypse, and the Unmaking of America (Little, Brown, 2026) [ 5 ] [ 6 ]

Tracing an evangelical obsession with the end times

Chris Jennings

End of Days
Ruby Ridge, the apocalypse, and the unmaking of America 384pp. Little, Brown. $30.
Why are Americans so drawn to conspiracy theories? In an age of QAnon and election denialism, the question has taken on renewed urgency. In End of Days , Chris Jennings’s lively account of the deadly confrontation between federal agents and the Weaver family at Ruby Ridge in 1992, he offers a compelling answer: the rise of “apocalyptic faith”, a mutant strain of evangelical Protestantism premissed on the conviction that the end of the world is imminent.
The broad outlines of the episode are familiar. In August 1992, federal agents surrounded the remote Idaho cabin of Randy Weaver, a Christian survivalist who had failed to appear in court on relatively minor firearms charges. The siege that followed lasted eleven days. By the time it ended, Weaver’s wife, Vicki, their son, Sammy, and the family dog were dead.
